plain_title: Microbes watermark their own DNA to shred invaders
plain_text: Bacteria methylate short password sequences on their own chromosome and chop up any un-watermarked viral DNA that injects itself inside.
source: Arber & Linn (1969) Annu. Rev. Biochem. 38:467; Roberts et al. (2015) Nucleic Acids Res. 43:D298
note: The simplest molecular self-versus-non-self check; biotechnology later used restriction enzymes to launch recombinant DNA.

milestone: CRISPR-Cas heritable viral DNA spacer memory
plain_title: Bacteria paste viral mugshots into their own genome
plain_text: About half of bacteria and almost all archaea snip 30-letter pieces of invading viruses into their own DNA, passing a genetic hit-list to their descendants.
mechanism: Cas1-Cas2 spacer integration + crRNA-guided Cas nuclease interference
source: Barrangou et al. (2007) Science 315:1709; Mojica et al. (2005) J. Mol. Evol. 60:174; Koonin, Makarova & Zhang (2017) Curr. Opin. Microbiol. 37:67
note: True Lamarckian-style heritable acquired immunity: captured viral spacers persist across thousands of bacterial generations.

milestone: Ancestral CBASS / cGAS-STING & viperin antiviral sensors
plain_title: Human antiviral alarms began inside bacteria
plain_text: Key alarm proteins that human cells use today to spot loose viral DNA in their fluid evolved billions of years earlier inside bacteria fighting phages.
mechanism: Cyclic dinucleotide second-messenger alarm -> abortive infection or interferon-pathway precursor
source: Morehouse et al. (2020) Nature 586:429; Bernheim et al. (2021) Nature 589:120; Wein & Sorek (2022) Nat. Rev. Microbiol. 20:696
note: Demonstrates deep evolutionary continuity between prokaryotic phage defense and mammalian innate immunity.

milestone: Eukaryotic RNA interference (Dicer / Argonaute) viral silencing
plain_title: Chopping double-stranded viral RNA into search guides
plain_text: Plants, fungi and invertebrates dice invading double-stranded viral RNA into 21-letter guides that hunt down and slice matching viral messages.
mechanism: Dicer dsRNA cleavage -> 21–24 nt siRNA loaded into Argonaute slicer
source: Fire et al. (1998) Nature 391:806; Ding & Voinnet (2007) Cell 130:413
note: In plants and C. elegans, mobile small RNAs spread antiviral silencing across the whole organism.

milestone: Metazoan phagocytes, Toll-like & NLR pattern receptors
plain_title: Roving guard cells with hardwired germ detectors
plain_text: Early animals deploy crawling amoeba-like cells studded with germline-encoded receptors that recognise conserved bacterial cell walls and flagellin.
mechanism: Pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP) recognition + phagocytosis + antimicrobial peptides
source: Metchnikoff (1893); Srivastava et al. (2010) Nature 466:720; Brennan & Gilmore (2018) Nat. Rev. Immunol. 18:705
note: Fast (minutes to hours) and shared across animals, with plant NLR resistance proteins evolving a striking convergent architecture.

plain_title: Lampreys invent a second antibody system from scratch
plain_text: Jawless lampreys and hagfish have no antibodies like ours; instead they stitch leucine-rich gene pieces into billions of curved receptors on two lymphocyte types.
representative_system: Petromyzon marinus (sea lamprey VLRA / VLRB / VLRC)
mechanism: Cytidine-deaminase-driven somatic assembly of leucine-rich repeat cassettes
source: Pancer et al. (2004) Nature 430:174; Boehm et al. (2012) Annu. Rev. Immunol. 30:203
note: Proves somatic combinatorial immunity evolved twice independently in early vertebrates.

milestone: Jawed-vertebrate RAG1/2 V(D)J recombination & B/T memory
plain_title: Shuffling DNA inside blood cells to anticipate unseen germs
plain_text: Sharks and all jawed vertebrates co-opted a jumping gene to cut and paste antibody segments, generating tens of billions of detectors and keeping memory cells for life.
representative_system: Cartilaginous & bony fishes to mammals (B cells, T cells, MHC)
mechanism: RAG1/2 V(D)J somatic recombination + AID hypermutation + germinal-center clonal selection
source: Tonegawa (1983) Nature 302:575; Agrawal, Eastman & Schatz (1998) Nature 394:744; Flajnik & Kasahara (2010) Nat. Rev. Genet. 11:47
note: Potential theoretical V(D)J junctional diversity exceeds 10^14; an individual human carries ~10^11–10^12 lymphocytes (~10^8–10^10 distinct clonotypes at once).

milestone: Mammalian placental tolerance & maternal IgG/IgA transfer
plain_title: Mothers lend newborns their immune memory
plain_text: Placental mammals suppress rejection of a genetically half-foreign fetus while passing decades of maternal antibodies across the placenta and in colostrum milk.
representative_system: Eutherian mammals (FcRn placental IgG + secretory IgA milk)
mechanism: Regulatory T-cell fetal tolerance + neonatal FcRn receptor antibody transport
source: Samstein et al. (2012) Cell 150:29; Palmeira et al. (2012) Clin. Dev. Immunol. 2012:985646
note: Bridges the newborn's vulnerable first months while its own lymphocyte repertoire learns the outside world.

milestone: Variolation, Jennerian vaccination & global smallpox eradication
plain_title: Training immune memory safely before the real plague arrives
plain_text: Exposing the immune system to a mild relative or weakened pathogen builds lifelong memory cells—eradicating smallpox worldwide by 1980.
mechanism: Deliberate antigen priming of long-lived memory B and T cells + herd-immunity threshold
source: Jenner (1798) Inquiry into the Variolae Vaccinae; Fenner et al. (1988) Smallpox and its Eradication, WHO
note: Smallpox remains the first human infectious disease driven to planetary extinction through shared public-health memory.

plain_title: Brewing one pure molecular antibody by the kilogram
plain_text: Fusing one antibody-making B cell with an immortal myeloma cell lets laboratories mass-produce a single precision antibody against a chosen target.
mechanism: Single-clone B-cell immortalization & recombinant humanized IgG biologics
note: Turned vertebrate antibody specificity into targeted therapies for cancer, autoimmune disease and viral neutralization.

milestone: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR-T) living cell therapy
plain_title: Reprogramming a patient's T cells to hunt cancer
plain_text: Doctors harvest a patient's own T cells, splice in a synthetic tumour-homing receptor gene, and infuse living hunter cells that multiply inside the body.
representative_system: Autologous CAR-T engineered lymphocytes (2017 FDA approval)
mechanism: Ex-vivo lentiviral/CRISPR receptor engineering of cytotoxic T lymphocytes
source: June, O'Connor, Kawalekar, Ghassemi & Milone (2018) Science 359:1361
note: Decade-long remissions show engineered CAR-T cells persisting as a living surveillance clone.

plain_title: Compiling digital sequences into human immune memory in weeks
plain_text: Wrapped in tiny fat droplets, synthetic pseudouridine messenger RNA slips past innate alarms to teach cells a viral protein within days of reading a pathogen's genome.
mechanism: N1-methylpseudouridine mRNA + ionizable lipid nanoparticle -> host ribosomal antigen expression
source: Karikó et al. (2005) Immunity 23:165; Polack et al. (2020) N. Engl. J. Med. 383:2603; Baden et al. (2021) N. Engl. J. Med. 384:403
note: Vaccine design moved from viral genome sequence online (Jan 2020) to first clinical batch in 42 days.
